comment: JSONTestSuite's test_parsing files, byte for byte at the pinned commit under app/specs/oracle/json-test-suite/test_parsing: the validation oracle for what a JSON parser must refuse (RFC 8259), and so for what the canonical form (RFC 8785, whose input must be I-JSON, RFC 7493) refuses. The suite names each file by its verdict: n_ must be refused, y_ must be accepted, i_ is left to the parser. Held here: every n_ file that is UTF-8 and fits the snapshot guest's 2048-byte request (174 of 188; 12 are not UTF-8, which an acceptance vector cannot carry, and 2 are larger than the request bound), and the files the suite names as lone or broken surrogates (10 i_ files), numbers whose exponent overflows a double (5 i_ files) and duplicated names (2 y_ files), which RFC 8785 sections 3.1, 3.2.2.2 and 3.2.2.3 require to be refused. SHA256SUMS lists each file in sha256sum's format and is written from the files by generators/transition's jsonsuitesums (GN-01 fails when a file changes, is added or is removed); generators/snapshot's lockcheck holds SHA256SUMS and the licence to the hashes below.
standard: RFC 8259 The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format, IETF; RFC 7493 The I-JSON Message Format; RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme
